images.title: Every 10 folds multiply by 1024
images.purpose: Shows that the thickness at fold 0, fold 10 and fold 20 grows by the same factor 1024 each time.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One long horizontal line across the middle with three large dots on it, and two big arcs above the line joining neighbouring dots.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal grey line across the frame. Exactly 3 large teal (#0072B2) dots sit on the line, evenly spaced: left, centre and right. Under the dots, in order, the labels 'fold 0', 'fold 10', 'fold 20'. Just above each dot, in order, the labels '0.001 cm', '1.024 cm', '1048.576 cm'. Exactly 2 large amber (#E69F00) arcs above the line, one from the left dot to the centre dot and one from the centre dot to the right dot, each with an arrowhead at its right end and the label '× 1024' at its top. No other marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Any 10 folds multiply the thickness by the same 1024: this is multiplicative growth.
images.description: Shows that the thickness at fold 0, fold 10 and fold 20 grows by the same factor 1024 each time.
images.teaching_notes: The label '× 1024' appears twice. Contrast with adding: the jumps are equal multiplications, not equal additions.

image_decisions.why: The picture makes multiplicative growth visible: equal steps of 10 folds always multiply by the same 1024.
